science-source-y8-safety-bay-2023-elemen.title: Year 8 Science — Elements and equations — Safety Bay 2023 (original assessment)
science-source-y8-safety-bay-2023-elemen.coverage: Original assessment MC with graphs and diagrams. All marked written tasks are retained in the bank, including isotope and rust-key corrections; original zero-mark Q11 is preserved as support.

questions.prompt: Matter that is only composed of one type of atom is called a(n) ……………….
questions.explanation: A. Element. An element contains only one type of atom.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following gases is a compound?
questions.explanation: B. CO2. CO₂ contains carbon and oxygen chemically combined; H₂, O₂ and N₂ are molecules of elements.

questions.prompt: The atomic number of an element tell us:
options: The number of neutrons in one atom
The number of protons in one atom
questions.explanation: D. The number of protons in one atom. Atomic number is the number of protons in an atom’s nucleus.

questions.prompt: The molecular formula for acetaldehyde is C2H4O. It contains the following atoms:
questions.explanation: C. 2x carbon, 4x hydrogen, 1x oxygen. C₂H₄O contains two carbon, four hydrogen and one oxygen atom in each molecule.

questions.prompt:
The electrical conductivity for four metals at different temperatures is shown in the graph below. According to this graph, the best conductor at 900°C is:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch07","id":"conductivity"}]}]
questions.explanation: C. Platinum. At 900 °C the platinum curve has the greatest conductivity on the supplied graph.

questions.prompt:
A student carries out an experiment to determine the effect of different types of salt solutions on an iron nail. Identify the purpose of the test tube containing the nail and water only.
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch07","id":"nail-control"}]}]
options: It allows a comparison between copper nitrate and copper sulfate
The water is added to test the strength of the nail
It is a control for the experiment
All of the answers are correct.
questions.explanation: C. It is a control for the experiment. The nail in water is the control, allowing comparison with nails in salt solutions.

questions.prompt:
Identify which of the following compounds is most likely to have molecules like that of the diagram below:
[LV-MEDIA:{"images":[{"pack":"repo-science-batch07","id":"molecule"}]}]
questions.explanation: D. Water, H2O. The model has three atoms, one central and two surrounding; among the options this matches H₂O.

questions.prompt: Identify the correct statement about the properties of compounds.
options: The properties of compounds are impossible to describe
The properties of compounds are different to those of the elements they are made from
The properties of compounds are the average properties of the elements that make them up
The properties of compounds are the same as the elements they are made from
questions.explanation: B. The properties of compounds are different to those of the elements they are made from. Compounds have properties different from those of their constituent elements.

questions.prompt: Tap water is best described as:
questions.explanation: C. A mixture. Tap water contains water and dissolved substances, so it is a mixture.

questions.prompt: Recall how the electron cloud and nucleus are held together
options: They have opposite electronic charge that attracts them together.
They have a similar electronic charge that attracts them together
They are chemically bonded to each other
The gravitational pull of the heavy nucleus attracts the light electrons
questions.explanation: A. They have opposite electronic charge that attracts them together.. The positively charged nucleus and negatively charged electrons attract electrostatically.
